newsitem.title: USA: Bristol-Myers seeks to accelerate growth.
newsitem.headline: Bristol-Myers seeks to accelerate growth.

text.p: Bristol Myers Squibb Co expects sales and earnings growth to continue to run ahead of the projected five-year industry mid-range average of five to eight percent, the company's chairman told shareholders on Tuesday.

"I want our growth rates to be at least at the industry average in the short term and at the top of the industry league in the long term. That means growing faster than we have been," Chairman Charles Heimbold said at the company's annual meeting.

Pointing to an 24 percent increase in Bristol Myer share price in the first quarter, compared with a 12 percent rise in the Standard and Poor's 500 index, Heimbold said he expected to extend an "aggressive stock repurchase program" under which the company has bought back 50 million shares since 1993.

The company will boost spending for advertising and promotion by $300 million this year and add 1,500 representatives to its sales force at an increased cost of $200 million. The moves are in response to the expected introduction of rival products for treating cholesterol, diabetes and cancer, Heimbold said.

Pharmaceuticals are 58 percent of Bristol Myers' business, and 55 percent of its unit volume is generated outside the United States. U.S. pharmaceutical sales were $9.7 billion out of a worldwide total of $17.1 billion, a spokeswoman said.

Heimbold said he expected to increase this year's productivity gains of $600 million in order to fund the expansion of global franchises, "small acquisitions" in the United States and elsewhere, and new product research.
Last week, Bristol Myers joined a genome research program with Affymetrix Inc and Millennium Pharmaceuticals Inc to develop genetic-based technologies for research and health care.
Heimbold said the company was "revamping and redefining" its research operations.
But when asked if positions would be eliminated as part of a restructuring, company spokesman Anthony Carter told Reuters, "Not that I know of at this point."
The company has set aside $2.2 billion, or $1.36 a share, to settle pending and future product liability claims, primarily those related to a class-action suit involving breast implants.
Drug store chains that opted out of a settlement agreement in a class-action antitrust suit last year have a potential $7.2 billion claim pending against Bristol Myers and other companies.

In other matters, shareholders approved management proposals for the re-election of three directors, for executive performance and stock incentive plans, and for the replenishing of shares distributed in a February stock split.
A majority of shares present at the meeting also approved a resolution by shareholder Evelyn Y. Davis recommending a return to holding annual elections of directors rather than a staggered board.
